content:
Right now, positivity does not support goals with forall quantifiers, which can be annoying.
Should we change this, i.e. positivity run on \forall i, foo i would be equivalent to the current intro i; positivity? This is fairly predictable, so does not seem like obvious scope creep to me.

Details:

  • I think this should do intro whenever the goal has explicit forall binders (but not more).
  • It would be nice to do this in a nested way, i.e. Real.rpow_nonneg (tsum_nonneg fun i ↦ by positivity) could become just positivity (example). Are there any downsides to doing so?

For the nesting, I'd think this should just be the responsibility of each individual posivity extension to support.

For intro on the original goal, I feel like if we support this, we may also want to support forall binders in hypotheses. Because otherwise people will complain that we cannot prove ∀ x, 0 < f x given h : ∀ x, 0 < f x.
